mainTopic: Do animals consecrated for the altar (קדשי מזבח) need העמדה והערכה (standing and valuation) when they are redeemed? This is the argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about the view of the רבנן.
overview: This amud is about whether animals given to the altar (קדשי מזבח) need העמדה והערכה, standing before a כהן and being valued, when they are redeemed. It opens by finishing a ברייתא that supports רבי יוחנן: the פסוק about an 'unofferable' animal means an altar animal with a permanent blemish, and the תורה requires standing and valuation for it. Then רב explains ריש לקיש's source from the words 'whether good or bad', which he reads as pointing to בדק הבית. For רבי יוחנן, the word 'אותה' leaves out an animal blemished from the start. The גמרא admits it cannot find a job for 'אותה' in the view of תנא דבי לוי. רב also gives רבי שמעון's opposite reading of the same פסוק, and the גמרא raises a difficulty on that reading too. Next, two ברייתות about consecrated animals that died are used to test רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש. Each side answers by explaining which case the ברייתא is about, and ריש לקיש even reverses the first ברייתא. The amud ends as רבי ירמיה begins a new challenge to ריש לקיש, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The verse about an unofferable animal means blemished animals
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks what the פסוק 'any animal of which they may not bring an offering' comes to teach. It answers that the פסוק is about blemished animals and teaches that they can be redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: So how do I explain the verse 'And if it be any animal of which they may not bring an offering to ה׳'? It is talking about blemished animals, and it teaches that they can be redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא that the גמרא brought as a proof for רבי יוחנן continues. It explains that the פסוק about an animal 'that cannot be offered' is talking about a בעל מום (blemished animal) that is being redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Standing and valuation for a non-kosher animal is already taught somewhere else. So this פסוק must be teaching something new. The ברייתא reads it as being about an animal that was fit for the altar but became blemished, and says such an animal can be redeemed through this process.

keyTerms.meaning: So how do I explain (this verse)? It asks what a פסוק teaches if its plain meaning is already covered elsewhere
Blemished animals, which cannot be brought on the altar
That they can be redeemed (exchanged for money so they lose their holiness)

phrases.english: So how do I explain
“And if it be any animal
of which they may not bring
an offering to ה׳”?
It is about blemished animals, teaching that they can be redeemed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מָה אֲנִי מְקַיֵּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא that was brought earlier on the דף as support for רבי יוחנן.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that according to the רבנן, altar animals also need העמדה והערכה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא from the ספרא explaining ויקרא 27:11.

steps.title: Only a permanent blemish, not a temporary one
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits the rule to an animal with a permanent blemish. The words 'that may not be offered' mean an animal that can never be offered, which leaves out one that could be offered tomorrow.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think a blemished animal can be redeemed even if its blemish is temporary. So the verse says 'of which they may not bring an offering', meaning one that cannot be offered at all. That leaves out this animal, which cannot be offered today but can be offered tomorrow.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a limit to the rule. Only an animal with a permanent blemish (מום קבוע) can be redeemed this way, not one with a temporary blemish (מום עובר).
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal with a temporary blemish will heal and become fit for the altar again, so it is not truly 'unofferable.' This detail matters for the proof. Only altar animals need a permanent blemish before they can be redeemed. בדק הבית animals can be redeemed even without any blemish.

keyTerms.meaning: A temporary blemish that will heal
One might have thought
The verse comes to teach
At all, ever

phrases.english: One might think they can be redeemed
even because of a temporary blemish?
Therefore the verse says
“of which they may not bring an offering”
meaning one that cannot be offered at all,
which leaves out this one, which cannot be offered today
but can be offered tomorrow.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל יִפָּדוּ עַל מוּם עוֹבֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows step 1 so that it covers only permanent blemishes.
steps.raayaObject: That the פסוק is about altar animals, since only they need a permanent blemish to be redeemed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The words אֲשֶׁר לֹא יַקְרִיבוּ מִמֶּנָּה in ויקרא 27:11.

steps.title: So the תורה requires standing and valuation for altar animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the proof. The פסוק is about a permanently blemished altar animal, and the תורה says to do העמדה והערכה for it. This supports רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Merciful One said: perform standing and valuation for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion of the proof. The animal in this פסוק is a blemished altar animal, and the תורה commands העמדה והערכה for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא required a permanent blemish, so the animal must be from קדשי מזבח. The same פסוק goes on to require standing and valuation. So altar animals are included in העמדה והערכה, just as רבי יוחנן said about the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the תורה or ה׳
Do for it
Standing the animal before a כהן and having him set its value

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא reads the פסוק about an 'unofferable animal' as a permanently blemished altar animal. Since the תורה requires העמדה והערכה for it, this supports רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: And the Merciful One said:
Perform standing and valuation for it.
phrases.notes: This points to the next words of the same פסוק: 'he shall set the animal before the כהן, and the כהן shall value it.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַחֲמָנָא עֲבֵיד לַהּ הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the permanent-blemish rule from step 2 to finish the proof for רבי יוחנן.
steps.raayaObject: According to the רבנן, altar animals are redeemed with העמדה והערכה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא, together with the command in the פסוק to stand and value the animal.

steps.title: What is ריש לקיש's reason?
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל in the name of רב asks for the source of ריש לקיש's view. ריש לקיש holds that according to the רבנן, only בדק הבית animals were included in standing and valuation, not altar animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל said in the name of רב: What is the reason of ריש לקיש, who said that according to the רבנן, animals consecrated for Temple upkeep were included in standing and valuation, but animals consecrated for the altar were not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the other side of the argument. רב גידל asks what source ריש לקיש has for saying that the רבנן did not include altar animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion supported רבי יוחנן. This step opens a new line: finding a פסוק behind ריש לקיש's view. In his view, the רבנן applied standing and valuation only to קדשי בדק הבית.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Things consecrated for the upkeep of the בית המקדש, not for the altar
Animals consecrated to be brought on the altar
Included in

phrases.english: Rav Giddel said that Rav said:
What is the reason of Reish Lakish,
who said that according to the Rabbis
animals consecrated for Temple upkeep were
included in standing and valuation,
but animals consecrated for the altar were not
included in standing and valuation?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the proof for רבי יוחנן to explaining ריש לקיש's opposite view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for ריש לקיש's view that, according to the רבנן, only בדק הבית animals need העמדה והערכה.

steps.title: The source: 'whether good or bad'
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש's source is the פסוק 'And the כהן shall value it, whether good or bad.' This shows the valuation is about an animal that may be unblemished, which fits only בדק הבית animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the verse says: 'And the כהן shall value it, whether it be good or bad.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב גידל answers his own question with a פסוק. 'Whether good or bad' means the valuation applies to animals with or without a blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An altar animal can only be redeemed if it is blemished ('bad'). A בדק הבית animal can be redeemed even when it is perfect ('good'). Since the פסוק includes 'good' animals too, ריש לקיש says it must be talking about קדשי בדק הבית.

keyTerms.meaning: Because the verse says
And he shall value
Whether good or bad, meaning unblemished or blemished

steps.confusionAlert: 'Good or bad' here does not mean a high or low price. It means an animal without a blemish or with one. That is why it points to בדק הבית animals.

phrases.english: Because the verse says:
“And the priest shall value it,
whether it be good or bad.”

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר קְרָא וְהֶעֱרִיךְ הַכֹּהֵן אוֹתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words בֵּין טוֹב וּבֵין רָע show that the valuation covers unblemished animals too. That fits only בדק הבית animals, so altar animals are not included according to the רבנן.

steps.title: Finishing ריש לקיש's proof: 'Good or bad' points to בדק הבית
steps.stepSummary: Something whose law is the same whether it is good or bad is a בדק הבית animal. The word 'אותה' leaves out altar animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: What kind of thing has no difference between good and bad? It must be animals given to בדק הבית. And the פסוק says 'it' to leave out animals given to the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining how ריש לקיש reads the פסוק from Step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בדק הבית animal has the same holiness whether it is blemished or not, so 'good or bad' makes no difference to it. That is the case the פסוק is describing. The extra word 'אותה' ('it') then limits the rule to that case and leaves out altar animals.

keyTerms.meaning: Divided, meaning the law is different in different cases
'You must say', which brings in the only possible answer
Things given to pay for the upkeep of the בית המקדש
Animals given to be brought on the altar
To exclude, or leave out

phrases.english: What is an item that is not divided
between good and bad?

phrases.aramaic: הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר: זֶה קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת,
phrases.english: You must say: this is items consecrated for Temple maintenance,
and the verse states "it"
to exclude items consecrated for the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיזֶהוּ דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ חָלוּק בֵּין טוֹב לְרַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer that began in Step 5
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Good or bad' means something whose law is the same either way, which is בדק הבית. 'אותה' leaves out altar animals.

steps.title: For רבי יוחנן, what does 'it' leave out?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן includes altar animals in the rule. So the גמרא asks what the limiting word 'אותה' leaves out for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יוחנן, what does 'it' come to leave out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns back to רבי יוחנן and asks what the word 'אותה' does in his reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ריש לקיש, 'אותה' neatly leaves out altar animals. רבי יוחנן holds that altar animals do need standing and valuation, so he cannot use the word that way. He still needs it to leave out something.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It', an extra word that limits the rule
What?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan,
"it" comes to exclude what?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, אוֹתָהּ לְמַעוֹטֵי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the other side reads the same word that ריש לקיש just used
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word 'אותה' leaves out according to רבי יוחנן

steps.title: It leaves out an animal that was blemished from the start
steps.stepSummary: For רבי יוחנן, 'אותה' leaves out an animal that already had a blemish when it was given to the altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to leave out an animal that was blemished from the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that for רבי יוחנן, 'אותה' leaves out an animal that was blemished before it was given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some altar animals were fine when they were given and became blemished later. Those need standing and valuation. An animal that was already blemished when it was given is left out of the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that was blemished from the start, before it was given

phrases.english: To exclude an animal blemished from the outset.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַעוֹטֵי בַּעַל מוּם מֵעִיקָּרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 7
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'אותה' leaves out an animal that was blemished from the start.

steps.title: תנא דבי לוי includes everything, so what does 'it' leave out?
steps.stepSummary: Levi taught that everything needs standing and valuation, even an animal blemished from the start, a wild animal, or birds. But then the word 'אותה' has nothing to leave out. The גמרא admits this is a difficulty.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the תנא of Levi's school? He said that even an animal blemished from the start needs standing and valuation. Levi taught: everything needed standing and valuation, even an animal blemished from the start. Levi also taught in his ברייתא: even a wild animal, and even birds. But the פסוק says 'it'! This is a difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the view of תנא דבי לוי, who includes everything. If he leaves nothing out, what does the word 'אותה' do? The question stays unanswered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 8 used up the word 'אותה' on an animal that was blemished from the start. Levi includes even that animal, and even wild animals and birds. So his view leaves the word with no job, and the גמרא ends with קשיא, an open difficulty.

keyTerms.meaning: The teacher of Levi's school of ברייתות
Standing the animal before the כהן, and having him set its value
A wild animal, which can never be brought as a קרבן
'It is difficult'. The question stays open with no answer.

steps.confusionAlert: Here קשיא does not reject Levi's teaching. It only means the גמרא could not find a job for the word 'אותה' in his view.

phrases.english: But according to the tanna of the school of Levi,
who said that even an animal blemished from the outset
is included in standing and valuation,
as Levi taught:
Everything was included in standing and valuation,
even an animal blemished from the outset,
and so too Levi taught in his baraita:
even an undomesticated animal, and even birds,
but isn't it written "it"!
phrases.notes: The point is that 'it' should leave something out, yet Levi leaves out nothing.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְתַנָּא דְּבֵי לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer in Step 8 cannot work for Levi's view
steps.kashyaTarget: תנא דבי לוי's view that everything needs standing and valuation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If even an animal blemished from the start, wild animals and birds are all included, the limiting word 'אותה' leaves out nothing.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יוחנן, 'אותה' leaves out an animal blemished from the start. For Levi, who includes everything, the word has no job. That stays an open קשיא.

steps.title: What is רבי שמעון's source?
steps.stepSummary: רב asks for the source of רבי שמעון's view. רבי שמעון holds that only altar animals need standing and valuation, not בדק הבית animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: What is the reason of רבי שמעון? He said that altar animals needed standing and valuation, and בדק הבית animals did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to רבי שמעון from the משנה and asks where his view comes from. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's view is the exact opposite of ריש לקיש's reading of the רבנן. So the גמרא needs a source that reads the same פסוק the other way.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason, or source?

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon, who said

phrases.aramaic: קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה,
phrases.english: that items consecrated for the altar were included in standing and valuation,
but items consecrated for Temple maintenance were not?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about the opinion of רבי שמעון
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק behind רבי שמעון's view that only altar animals need standing and valuation

steps.title: For רבי שמעון, 'good or bad' points to altar animals
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון reads 'good or bad' as something whose law changes with a blemish, which is altar animals. So 'אותה' leaves out בדק הבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And the כהן shall value it, whether good or bad.' What kind of thing has a difference between good and bad? It must be altar animals. And the פסוק says 'it' to leave out בדק הבית.
steps.whatsHappening: רב shows that רבי שמעון reads the same words as ריש לקיש did, but in the opposite way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An altar animal's law changes with a blemish: if it is unblemished it is brought on the altar, and if it is blemished it is redeemed. So 'good or bad' fits altar animals. Then 'אותה' leaves out בדק הבית, which is the reverse of ריש לקיש's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he shall value', meaning the כהן sets its price
Whether good (unblemished) or bad (blemished)

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides use the same words, 'good or bad', but they read them in opposite ways. ריש לקיש says they mean 'no difference', which is בדק הבית. רבי שמעון says they mean 'there is a difference', which is altar animals.
steps.whatToRemember: The argument comes down to how to read 'good or bad'. If it means the law is the same either way, it points to בדק הבית. If it means the law is different, it points to altar animals. In each reading, 'אותה' leaves out the other kind.

phrases.english: For the verse states:
"And the priest shall value it
whether good or bad,"
What is an item that is divided
between good and bad?
You must say: this is items consecrated for the altar,
and the verse states "it"
to exclude Temple maintenance items.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר קְרָא וְהֶעֱרִיךְ הַכֹּהֵן אוֹתָהּ בֵּין טוֹב וּבֵין רָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Good or bad' means something whose law changes with a blemish, which is altar animals. 'אותה' leaves out בדק הבית.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how one פסוק can support two opposite rulings, depending on how you read 'good or bad'.

steps.title: The wording of the פסוק does not fit רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: If 'good or bad' points to a difference between the two kinds of animals, the פסוק should have said 'between good and bad'. The גמרא leaves this as an unanswered difficulty for רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the פסוק should have said 'between good and bad'! This is a difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי שמעון's reading of the פסוק from step 11. It says his reading does not fit the exact words the פסוק uses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון said 'good or bad' means an animal whose law changes with a blemish. If the תורה meant to point to that difference, it would have said 'between good and bad'. The actual wording, 'whether good or whether bad', sounds like both are treated the same, so the גמרא calls it a קשיא and moves on.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your reading is right)
It should have said
A difficulty that is left unanswered

phrases.english: If so,
it should have said 'between good and bad'!
phrases.notes: The פסוק actually says 'בין טוב ובין רע' (ויקרא 27:12), which sounds like both get the same law.

phrases.english: It is a difficulty.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, בֵּין טוֹב לְרָע מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the derivation רבי שמעון gave in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's reading of 'good or bad' as pointing to altar animals
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Wording that is meant to show a difference would read 'between good and bad'. The phrasing 'whether good or whether bad' suggests both are equal.

steps.title: A ברייתא about consecrated animals that died
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: if consecrated animals die, unblemished ones are buried and blemished ones are redeemed. That rule is only for altar animals. With בדק הבית animals, all are buried.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: If consecrated animals died, unblemished ones are buried and blemished ones are redeemed. When is this said? With altar animals. But with בדק הבית animals, both unblemished and blemished ones are buried.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge by quoting the first opinion of a ברייתא. The actual attack comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dead animal cannot stand up to be valued. So if a kind of animal needs standing and valuation, it cannot be redeemed once it dies and must be buried. The ברייתא lets blemished altar animals be redeemed after death, which suggests they do not need standing and valuation.

keyTerms.meaning: They shall be buried
They shall be redeemed
Animals consecrated to be offered on the altar
Things consecrated for the upkeep of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
If unblemished ones died, they shall be buried,
and blemished ones shall be redeemed.
In what case are these words said?
With animals consecrated for the altar,
but with animals consecrated for Temple upkeep,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין תְּמִימִין בֵּין בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִים יִקָּבֵרוּ.
phrases.english: both unblemished and blemished ones shall be buried.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the difficulty on רבי שמעון to a new challenge from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that altar animals need standing and valuation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only. The ברייתא's first opinion lets blemished altar animals be redeemed after death, so it seems they do not need standing.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's opinion and the refutation of רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון in the ברייתא treats altar and בדק הבית animals the same: unblemished ones are buried and blemished ones are redeemed. The גמרא then says the first part of the ברייתא refutes רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: both altar animals and בדק הבית animals, if unblemished, are buried, and if blemished, are redeemed. This is a refutation of רבי יוחנן from the first part!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא with רבי שמעון's opinion. Then it makes its attack: the first opinion seems to disprove רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן held that, according to the רבנן, altar animals also need standing and valuation, so they should be buried once they die. But the first part of the ברייתא, which is the רבנן's view, says blemished altar animals that died are redeemed. That contradicts רבי יוחנן, so the גמרא calls it a תיובתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this and that (the same law for both)
A strong refutation
The first part of a teaching

steps.confusionAlert: The refutation comes from the first part of the ברייתא (the רבנן), not from רבי שמעון's part. רבי יוחנן was explaining the view of the רבנן.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Both animals consecrated for the altar
and animals consecrated for Temple upkeep:
unblemished ones shall be buried,
blemished ones shall be redeemed.
This is a refutation of Rabbi Yoḥanan from the first part!
phrases.notes: The first part is the רבנן's opinion, which lets blemished altar animals be redeemed after they die.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מֵרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 13 and states the attack.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that, for the רבנן, altar animals need standing and valuation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An animal that needs standing cannot be redeemed once it dies. The רבנן let dead blemished altar animals be redeemed, so for them altar animals must not need standing.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן answers: an animal blemished from the start
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the ברייתא is talking about an animal that was already blemished when it was consecrated. Such an animal does not need standing and valuation, so it can be redeemed after it dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן can tell you: What case are we dealing with here? An animal that was blemished from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן by narrowing the case in the ברייתא. It is about an animal that had a blemish from the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8 we learned that, for רבי יוחנן, the word 'אותה' leaves out an animal that was blemished when it was given to the altar. So that animal does not need standing and can be redeemed even after death. An altar animal that got a blemish later still needs standing and would be buried.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (used to narrow the case)
An animal that was blemished from the start, before it was consecrated

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יוחנן, altar animals need standing and valuation. The one exception is an animal that was blemished from the start, and that is the case the ברייתא is talking about.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan can say to you:
What case are we dealing with here?
With an animal that was blemished from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכָא בְמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the refutation in step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is talking about any blemished altar animal, which would mean altar animals never need standing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is talking only about an animal that was blemished from the start. That animal is left out of standing and valuation by 'אותה', so רבי יוחנן's view stands.

steps.title: Logic supports reading the ברייתא as an animal blemished from the start
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא were about an animal consecrated first and blemished later, רבי שמעון should have argued. Since he does not, it must be about an animal blemished from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense. If you say the animals were consecrated before they got blemished, רבי שמעון should argue about it. So we must learn that it is talking about an animal that was blemished from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a logical proof that רבי יוחנן's answer in Step 15 is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that altar animals need standing and valuation, so a blemished altar animal that dies after being consecrated healthy would have to be buried. Yet in the ברייתא he agrees that blemished animals are redeemed. That only works if the animal was blemished from the start, since such an animal never needed standing and valuation.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it is logical: a phrase that adds support to the previous answer
Their consecration came before their blemish
An animal that was blemished from the start, before it was consecrated
He should disagree

phrases.english: So too it is logical,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי תֵּימָא שֶׁקָּדַם הֶקְדֵּישָׁן אֶת מוּמָן —
phrases.english: for if you say that their consecration came before their blemish,
then רבי שמעון should disagree about it,
rather, must we not learn from this
that it is about an animal blemished from the start?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer רבי יוחנן gave in Step 15
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's reading that the ברייתא is about an animal blemished from the start
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון's silence in the ברייתא, which would make no sense if the animal had been blemished after consecration

steps.title: Does this reading refute ריש לקיש?
steps.stepSummary: If the רבנן let the animal be redeemed only because it was blemished from the start, then one blemished after consecration would be buried. That goes against ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, let us say this is a refutation of ריש לקיש!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the new reading against ריש לקיש, who holds that for the רבנן altar animals do not need standing and valuation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ruling of the רבנן is limited to animals blemished from the start, the hidden message is that animals blemished after consecration are buried. That would mean the רבנן do require standing and valuation for altar animals, which is the opposite of ריש לקיש's view.

keyTerms.meaning: A strong refutation that knocks down a view
Let us say: introduces a suggested conclusion

phrases.english: But then, let us say
it is a refutation of ריש לקיש!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reading proven in Step 16 to attack the other side
steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לֵימָא תֶּיהְוֵי תְּיוּבְתֵּיהּ דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that for the רבנן, altar animals do not need standing and valuation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Limiting redemption to animals blemished from the start implies that animals blemished after consecration are buried, which contradicts ריש לקיש.

steps.title: ריש לקיש reads the ברייתא as consecrated first, blemished later
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the ברייתא is about animals that were consecrated first and blemished later. Then the רבנן's ruling that they are redeemed fits his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש explains the ברייתא as talking about animals whose consecration came before their blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends ריש לקיש by giving him a different reading of the case in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, the רבנן allow redeeming even an animal that was healthy when consecrated. That matches ריש לקיש, who holds that for the רבנן altar animals do not need standing and valuation.

keyTerms.meaning: He sets it up as: explains a source as talking about a specific case

phrases.english: ריש לקיש explains it as talking about
a case where their consecration came before their blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge to ריש לקיש in Step 17
steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מוֹקֵים לַהּ בְּשֶׁקָּדַם הֶקְדֵּישָׁן אֶת מוּמָן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about an animal blemished from the start, which suggests the רבנן bury one blemished later.
steps.terutzMaskana: For ריש לקיש, the ברייתא is about an animal blemished after consecration, and the רבנן still let it be redeemed.

steps.title: Then why doesn't רבי שמעון argue?
steps.stepSummary: If the case is an animal consecrated first and blemished later, רבי שמעון should argue and say it is buried.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, רבי שמעון should argue about it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back the same logic from Step 16, this time against ריש לקיש's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that altar animals need standing and valuation. So in ריש לקיש's case he should require burial. But in the ברייתא he agrees that blemished animals are redeemed.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: introduces a problem that follows from the last answer

phrases.english: If so,
רבי שמעון should argue about it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given for ריש לקיש in Step 18
steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, נִיפְלוֹג רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן עֲלַהּ
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's reading that the ברייתא is about an animal blemished after consecration
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון requires standing and valuation for altar animals, so in that case he would have to argue and require burial.

steps.title: ריש לקיש has the ברייתא reversed
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש holds a reversed version of the ברייתא and quotes it: animals that died are buried whether healthy or blemished. That is for altar animals, but בדק הבית animals are redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש reverses the ברייתא. And this is how he raises his challenge, from a different ברייתא: If they died, whether healthy or blemished, they are buried. When is this said? With altar animals. But with בדק הבית animals, they are redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ריש לקיש learns the first ברייתא with its rulings reversed, so in his version רבי שמעון does argue and the question falls away. Then ריש לקיש raises his own challenge against רבי יוחנן from a different ברייתא, which the גמרא begins to quote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reversing the first ברייתא answers step 19: in ריש לקיש's version רבי שמעון does argue about blemished altar animals. The quoted lines are a second ברייתא, where the רבנן bury dead altar animals and redeem בדק הבית animals. ריש לקיש uses it to attack רבי יוחנן, and it continues in step 21.

keyTerms.meaning: He reverses it: he reads the source with its rulings switched around
A different ברייתא (another collection of teachings)

steps.confusionAlert: Two different things happen here. First, ריש לקיש reverses the first ברייתא. Second, he quotes a different ברייתא to challenge רבי יוחנן. The lines quoted here come from that second ברייתא, not from the reversed first one.

phrases.english: ריש לקיש reverses it,
phrases.notes: He learns the first ברייתא with its rulings switched, so there רבי שמעון does argue.

phrases.english: and this is how he raises his challenge
from a different baraita:

phrases.aramaic: מֵתוּ, בֵּין תְּמִימִין בֵּין בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין —
phrases.english: If they died, whether healthy or blemished,
they are buried.
When is this said?
phrases.notes: The square bracket marks words that the corrected wording adds here.

phrases.english: With altar animals,
but with animals for the upkeep of the בית המקדש,
they are redeemed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מֵיפָךְ אָפֵיךְ, וְהָכִי מוֹתֵיב מִמְּכִילְתָּא אַחֲרִיתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 19 by saying ריש לקיש had a different version of the ברייתא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different version of the source (reversed text)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone learns the ברייתא the same way, so ריש לקיש's reading leaves רבי שמעון's silence unexplained.
steps.terutzMaskana: ריש לקיש learns the first ברייתא reversed, so רבי שמעון does argue there. He then brings a different ברייתא as his own challenge against רבי יוחנן.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a whole argument can depend on which version of a ברייתא a sage had, not only on how he reads it.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's view on dead Temple-maintenance animals
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: רבי שמעון says unblemished קדשי בדק הבית that died are buried, and blemished ones are redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: unblemished animals are buried, and blemished animals can be redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא with the opinion of רבי שמעון. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון argues only about animals given to בדק הבית. He splits them: a healthy animal that died is buried, but a blemished one can still be redeemed. He says nothing here about קדשי מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: Unblemished, healthy animals
Blemished animals
They must be buried
They can be redeemed (bought back with money)

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Unblemished ones shall be buried,
phrases.notes: He is talking about animals given to בדק הבית that died.

phrases.english: and blemished ones shall be redeemed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא being used to test the two אמוראים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, dead unblemished בדק הבית animals are buried, while blemished ones are redeemed.

steps.title: The ending of the ברייתא seems to refute רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the ending of the ברייתא disproves רבי יוחנן, since the רבנן there let dead קדשי בדק הבית be redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of רבי יוחנן from the latter part!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן using the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says that according to the רבנן, בדק הבית animals also need standing and valuation, so once they die they must be buried. But the end of the רבנן's words in this ברייתא says dead בדק הבית animals are redeemed. So the ברייתא seems to contradict him.

keyTerms.meaning: A strong refutation: a source that seems to disprove a view completely
The latter part of a source

phrases.english: A refutation of Rabbi Yochanan from the latter clause!
phrases.notes: The latter clause is the רבנן's ruling that בדק הבית animals that died are redeemed.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִסֵּיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא just quoted against רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that, for the רבנן, all consecrated animals (including בדק הבית) need standing and valuation and are buried if they die
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא has the רבנן redeeming dead בדק הבית animals. Yet רבי יוחנן says they include בדק הבית in standing and valuation, so those animals should be buried.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the case is an animal blemished from the start
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the ברייתא is talking about an animal that was blemished before it was consecrated.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן can tell you: what case are we dealing with here? An animal that was blemished from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן defends himself by narrowing the case of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the animal already had a blemish when it was consecrated, it was only holy for its money value. That kind of animal can be redeemed even after it dies. So the רבנן's ruling in the ברייתא does not touch רבי יוחנן's case of an animal consecrated healthy.

keyTerms.meaning: "What are we dealing with here?" A formula that limits a source to a specific case
A blemish from the start, before the animal was consecrated

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan can say to you:
What are we dealing with here?
With an animal blemished from the outset.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הָכָא בְמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the תיובתא against רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סיפא is about any dead בדק הבית animal, so the רבנן always allow its redemption.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is only about an animal blemished before it was consecrated.

steps.title: Support: otherwise רבי שמעון should have argued
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports רבי יוחנן's reading: if the case were consecrated first and blemished later, רבי שמעון would have argued on the קדשי מזבח ruling too.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also reasonable, because if you say the case is where the consecration came before the blemish, רבי שמעון should argue on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings logical support for רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון argues only about בדק הבית, so it looks like he agrees with the רבנן about קדשי מזבח. That fits if the case is an animal blemished from the start. If it were an animal consecrated healthy and blemished later, we would expect רבי שמעון to argue there too.

keyTerms.meaning: "So too it is logical": the גמרא is bringing support
Their consecration came before their blemish
Let him argue / he should have argued

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable,
for if you say
it is where their consecration preceded their blemish —
Rabbi Shimon should disagree with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the answer just given for רבי יוחנן.
steps.raayaObject: That the ברייתא is about an animal blemished from the start
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון's silence about קדשי מזבח in the ברייתא

steps.title: Then the ברייתא refutes ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the ברייתא is about an animal blemished from the start, it should disprove ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, let us say it is a refutation of ריש לקיש!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns the challenge onto ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש holds the רבנן redeem dead קדשי מזבח even when the animal was consecrated healthy. If the ברייתא allows redemption only because the animal was blemished from the start, then an animal blemished later would be buried. That goes against ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: "But then": turns the argument in a new direction
"Shall we say?"

phrases.english: But then, let us say
it is a refutation of Reish Lakish!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לֵימָא תֶּיהְוֵי תְּיוּבְתֵּיהּ דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the reading that saved רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that the רבנן redeem dead קדשי מזבח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If redemption is allowed only for an animal blemished from the start, one blemished after consecration would not be redeemed, against ריש לקיש.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the case is consecrated first, blemished later
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that the ברייתא is about animals consecrated first and blemished later.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש can tell you: what case are we dealing with here? Where their consecration came before their blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש reads the ברייתא his own way to defend himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the case is an animal consecrated healthy and blemished later, then the רבנן's ruling that it is redeemed fits ריש לקיש exactly. He rejects the reading given for רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecration: making something holy
Came first, preceded
A blemish that makes an animal unfit for the altar

phrases.english: Reish Lakish can say to you:
What are we dealing with here —
where their consecration preceded their blemish.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: הָכָא בְמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about an animal blemished from the start, which disproves ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about an animal consecrated healthy and blemished later, which supports ריש לקיש.

steps.title: But then רבי שמעון should argue
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: if the case is consecrated first and blemished later, רבי שמעון should argue on the קדשי מזבח ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then רבי שמעון should argue on it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back the same logic from step 24, now aimed at ריש לקיש's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 showed that רבי שמעון's silence suggests the case is a blemish from the start. If ריש לקיש says otherwise, he must explain why רבי שמעון does not argue about קדשי מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: On it (on that ruling)

phrases.english: But Rabbi Shimon should disagree with it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנִיפְלוֹג רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן עֲלַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading ריש לקיש just gave.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's reading of the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the animal was consecrated healthy, רבי שמעון would be expected to argue, yet the ברייתא shows him arguing only about בדק הבית.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: רבי שמעון really does argue
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that רבי שמעון does indeed argue about קדשי מזבח too.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש can tell you: indeed, רבי שמעון does argue.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש accepts the point and says רבי שמעון argues on קדשי מזבח as well, even though the ברייתא does not spell it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש does not have to explain why רבי שמעון is silent. He says רבי שמעון's argument covers both kinds of consecrated animals, and the ברייתא just mentions it about בדק הבית. So the ברייתא no longer disproves ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: "Indeed, that is so": agreeing with the questioner's point
He disagrees

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא can fit both אמוראים: רבי יוחנן reads it as an animal blemished from the start, and ריש לקיש reads it as an animal consecrated first, with רבי שמעון arguing on קדשי מזבח too.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish can say to you:
Indeed, Rabbi Shimon does disagree.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: הָכִי נָמֵי דִּפְלִיג רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by accepting that רבי שמעון argues.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון agrees with the רבנן about קדשי מזבח, so the case must be a blemish from the start.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון argues about קדשי מזבח too; the ברייתא just mentions his view about בדק הבית.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה begins a question on ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה starts a question to רבי זירא about ריש לקיש, who says the רבנן hold קדשי מזבח were not included in העמדה והערכה, and begins quoting a source about קדשי מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said to רבי זירא: According to ריש לקיש, who says that according to the רבנן קדשי מזבח were not included in העמדה והערכה, and yet it is taught: "קדשי מזבח...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge against ריש לקיש. The question continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש says that according to the רבנן, the rule that a consecrated animal must be stood up and valued before redemption does not apply to קדשי מזבח. רבי ירמיה is about to quote a source about קדשי מזבח that seems to clash with this.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals consecrated to be offered on the altar
Standing and valuation: standing the animal before a כהן so it can be priced for redemption
Included in
"It teaches": introducing a source that seems to clash

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said to Rabbi Zeira:
According to Reish Lakish, who says that according to the Rabbis:
altar-consecrated animals were not
